title: Compact causal difference chain: sufficient physical state without redundant channels
coverage_gap: The original LL/HH factor coverage gap remains, but the released development results reveal no observed C/E failure for any initial candidate. They therefore do not justify inventing a failure-specific repair. The testable remaining design question is whether A1's redundant geometric conditioning is needed, or whether an invertible smaller representation can preserve its measured success with less representation and conditioning overhead.
reusable_regularity: Positions form a serial hand--stick--payload--goal chain; current chain geometry plus body displacements and orientation history is a sufficient coordinate system for the same causal raw state. A4 keeps the physical scales and world anchor of A1, removes duplicated previous chain snapshots and explicit link norms, and expresses the full transformation as a single fixed affine operation. This introduces a minimal-sufficient-state bias rather than a learned compression bottleneck or a new controller.
dependencies_preserved: Output 0:3 is current hand minus a support-only world-xy origin divided by 0.2 m; 3:6 is stick-hand divided by 0.05 m; 6:9 is payload-stick divided by 0.2 m; 9:12 is goal-payload divided by 0.1 m. These vectors reconstruct every current world position, including goal, and preserve absolute height and world axes.

Output 12:16 and 16:20 retain both current xyzw object quaternions with vector components scaled by 0.1 and scalar component unscaled. Output 20 is current aperture. Output 21:30 retains hand/stick/payload displacement from native previous state, in units of 0.01 m. Output 30 is aperture difference divided by 0.1. Output 31:35 and 35:39 retain native-previous quaternions. Previous body positions and aperture are reconstructed by subtraction; no declared physical field is removed.

The same 39-dimensional map is applied to each of the two whole observations. No last-history compression, episode clock, stage oracle, contact flag or future label is introduced. Displacement is a measured observation difference, not a prediction.

The tool point is the declared stick COM and payload point is the declared insertion site plus [0,.09,0]. Retained robot/world position, gravity and orientation preserve the available fixture dependencies. No unobserved geometry, obstacle map, planner or simulator data are used.

evidence_refs.source: development_feedback in the revision user message
evidence_refs.observation: A1, A2 and A3 each achieved 20/20 C and 20/20 E successes, with every cell at 1.0. Fixed-method latencies were A1=0.1028795154998079 s, A2=0.11209302950010169 s and A3=0.10644192000472685 s. Thus q3 is A1 by latency. Each C/E 95% binomial interval has reported lower endpoint 0.8388748419471806; the ceiling on this finite development set does not prove population-perfect success.

evidence_refs.source: submitted A1 design and implementation in this session
evidence_refs.observation: The selected 55-channel deterministic chain retained both pose snapshots, their explicit motion differences, and redundant link distances. A4 preserves its units, world anchor and native action semantics but removes representational redundancy.

evidence_refs.source: submitted A2 design and implementation in this session
evidence_refs.observation: The successful graph model included a compact 39-channel recoverable geometric skip. This supports testing a compact direct path, but is not an ablation proving the graph or its motion auxiliary loss unnecessary.
All support fitting remains confined to the exact ten listed demonstrations; no new evidence or training episodes are added.
Defines the 39 raw channels, explicit native previous state, scene-point semantics and world action4.
Observed body displacements distinguish stationary tool, lifting stick and subsequently moving payload, so A4 retains these signals explicitly rather than simply deleting the native previous state.
Real initial fixture/robot layout motivates retaining world anchors.
Real manipulation frame motivates the separate hand-tool-payload relations.
Real displaced-payload frame motivates preserving payload and goal as separate state roles.

expected_failure_signature: A4 is not claimed faster or equally successful before its formal evaluation. Although the map is invertible, the unchanged finite U-Net must now derive link lengths and previous relative errors itself. Reduced feature redundancy could make grasp/lift switching harder, producing new failures even with no information removed. Conversely, matching C/E success with lower fixed-method latency would support the compact representation hypothesis. Small observed timing changes may be noisy; final selection will use the frozen reported latency rule without extra benchmarking or retries. No A1--A3 observed failure is fabricated.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,39] from the common deployment observation
required_runtime_fields.support_fit: Population mean of current hand xy over exactly D_N obs[0:T], with world z origin zero, identical estimator to A1. The xy constant is serialized; a fixed 39x39 affine matrix and 39-vector offset are registered nonlearned buffers during build_modules and rebuilt on deployment. No learned parameters are fitted outside the common optimizer, and the common normalizer is not changed.
required_runtime_fields.action_semantics: Identity encode/decode of native [world_dx,world_dy,world_dz,gripper], not a rotated, residual or normalized action space. The host alone clips the world action cube, applies 0.01 m xyz scaling and executes four of sixteen actions at 80 Hz.

change_summary: One new revision training slot. Primary parent A1 supplies the selected deterministic relative/world bias, exact physical scales and action semantics. A2 contributes the compact recoverable direct-state representation idea; its learned graph and joint future-motion channels are not inherited. Compared with A1, replace 55 channels by a 39-channel full-rank affine state/difference map, remove three explicit norms and duplicate previous geometry, and retain individual motions plus all quaternion/aperture information. No A3 gate, no auxiliary loss, no learned encoder and no action-frame change. The single factory DP now has the same condition/action dimensions as B0, without changing the fixed U-Net recipe. A1--A3 are immutable; A4 is initialized and trained from scratch, not a checkpoint reuse. No structural repairs at authoring time.
